Then he went to his secretary on the same inquisitive errand; he was upon his diversions in Kent, which is generally practised by the gentlemen of business during the vacation. So that Charles is positive nothing can be don till next term and is satisfied no alteration of the order will be made, being there has bin no president of such a practice in that court. However as Charles was going out of town to visit some of his wife's relations for a week or ten days, I charged that he would call again the last thing he did both at the Keeper's and his secretary's to get information and give you an account, and att his return I shall take care to remind him. All this he gave me his word and hand should be don and every thing else that was necessary. I read him over the letter and desired of him to consider in time what further affidavits were necessary, so that timely notice might be given you. I gave him the answer to the affidavit. I received half a crown for postage, after which we parted. You have now I perceive drawn your sword and thrown away the scabbard. My best wishes attend you. And doubt not of your success, depending on the righteousness of your cause. In the next place, I must most earnestly recommend to you the giving in your account of the Chopwell waggon way without loss of time, though it were but in gross for timber so much, workmanship in another article, so that four or five heads will suffice; and give it into Mr Clavering for our accounts must be made up off hand and without that of yours they can't close that year's book. I therefore earnestly entreat you
will doe it and I shall reckon it a particular obligation laid upon ...
55 November 1st 1712

You have obliged me extremely by your two last. Just now I am sent for to meet Jack Headword att the Tavern to drink a token from Jimmy Clavering , a place I have scarce troubled since you left the town. This will oblige me to cut short. Therefore you will excuse if I write as a late author does, by sentences. No longer than yesterday's post, I had in a postscript to the Captain an order under my father's own hand for taking Urpeth upon the best terms. So shall meet Tom and Calverley both att the Tavern on Monday or Tuesday next in order to conclude if possible. I thank you for your kind offer in relation the disbursements of my 1/4. I acquiesce in what you judge most necessary about working or lying in the upper seams, about which you have a vast of trouble and scurvy usage. I could have wished that the terms for William Ramsay's way, as also through Team had bin thoroughly adjusted, for I shall find a tedious business off it if left to me to transact with him.
It is not becoming one in my circumstances to object against any thing he may think reasonable etc. I am concerned that the number 5 should not as yet have rewarded you for your London journey. I was an eye witness to the indefatigable pains you took in a service for which you did deserve a generous recompense and even without a demurr. Methinks it is copying after the public. I am sorry that my interest should be off disservice rather than otherwise to you att this time: and that a suspicion should be raised that I am playing into your hand when I only recommend to them to be mindful and not to neglect a person so capable of serving or otherwise distressing them in their business according as he is used. But a word to the wise is enough. Your scheme seems justly calculated about Bensham way leave and steath rooms. No objection have I to it but this; when it is known that you have taken all those and on supposition that you should even lay the Chief Justice on his back (which I hope you will be able to effect), yet say I, will not that give a colourable handle for bringing in and obtaining an Act for giving a reasonable compensation for all manner off way leaves ? I don't infer from thence that there is any just grounds to be given for so doing, yet reason does not att all times prevail, nay the best arguments are but indifferently heard in a crowd. I give only this touch for you to improve. I am glad to hear you have had the offer of Bucksnook ; it is a certain sign they grow sick of their undertaking. You would doe well to know the real terms on which she will be let, as also the party or parties that will join in the letting, for I am satisfied Brumell has the least share and that she is like a bastard whose mother can't give an account off the real father. In the next place you must be satisfied on what terms Sir John and others will let way leaves and att what price for the way as it now lies. They will certainly endeavour to deny you as much as possible. It is worth while likewise to consider if feasible to lay a waggon way from the pitts to the mount, for as it is their coals don't entirely answer the expectations off the markett by reason that they don't come as round as formerly. I thank you for your kind offer off letting me be concerned as a partner in whatever offers. You lay me under deep obligations, which under present circumstances I cannot tell how to rubb out. My time off appointment draws near. Have but time to thank you for the d's comical
adventure; to request secrecy in this as far as you think necessary, and therefore get Mr Ashley to frank for me; and so wish you success in your cause which is putt off till Tuesday or Thursday next and to all your family welfare and happiness. I remain ...
P.S. Read this if you can.
58 December 20th 1712

These great and lasting falls of snow will not allow me to alter my tone in regard to health and what discourages me much is it has affected our honest doctor to that degree that he is confined
to his bed, and none allowed to see him but the apothecary. However I can't forbear writing a line to my good friend, notwithstanding these afflictions, and inform him a little of what passes in relation to the matter on the anvil. It is near a week since young Whitfield delivered a paper book off a lease in form, which I read cursorily over and sent it to my father, whose indisposition would not allow him to look it over till the day before yesterday, with which he was not well pleased. The rent is there to commence from Candlemas. The lands he will not on any advanced rent let to us. Therefore we shall have a troublesome matter to adjust about damages. By this lease we are to pay 40s damage for heap room, with the addition of the word yearly; that we are to make ample satisfaction besides for way leaves and all spoil off ground for building hovels, stables, cottages and all other necessaries for the colliery, the like I believe was never heard off. In the next place they foist in a new covenenant that we shall not let or assign any part off the colliery to any without the privity and consent of the lessor first obtained in writing, on penalty of forfeiture of the lease; and several other strange unheard off clauses. On this my father called a council, whereof Dan Poyen was one and I the other. The question being putt what was most fitting to be done in this emergency, I proposed to send their paper book as also your instructions and lease to John Ord, with yours and the Captain's last remarks copied, and those heads that we had agreed to before and was to be the true foundation for a lease, and see if he could hammer out of both a lease that would be most to mutual advantage of both parties; that the harsh part of their paper book should be softened so as it may be advisable for the lessees to comply with. This was resolved upon nominee contradicent and accordingly the whole was putt yesterday into Mr Ord's hands, who promised to bring us a copy of such a lease he shall think proper we should insist on by Tuesday next. He says that several of the lands, as the Riding and others, are copyhold and consequently the bishop's royalty. By all which you may guess that our trouble is not ended, nay far from it, for I doe assure you that Tom is so positive that I doubt he will not relinquish a tittle; therefore must beg your further advice how we should act in this matter and how far. I don't know but that my father writes to the Captain by this post, but if he does not I desire you will communicate to the honest Captain the
contents of this letter. In the next place I must acquaint you that we had several meetings with the Billingsgate people but nothing is yet fixed upon with those vermin. They hang in a clan much firmer than the coal owners and are truer to each other; I doubt the harmony among the Gentlemen will not be long lived. My head and from thence to foot are full of pain, therefore excuse faults and hast from ...
59 January 1st 1712/13

Yours of the 23th ult. lies before me. Have weighed the account you give about wining off Urpeth . I must readily concur with you that the best method will be off attempting to get her to the dipp as far as you can, but with this caution that you be sure off a good roof (which may be easily discovered by the boring); otherwise you may depend that where there is but little roof and even that tender, the coal will prove mean and chargeable working, by reason you can't drive the bords to any breadth, and the insett into a colliery is much the same as the outburst off the seam, both being fagg ends and of no intrinsic value. But I know you have the ablest off heads to determine, to whose judgement I perfectly submit, as also to yours about building the steath dyke with stone, and if you get that done for £15 a keel birth it will be a penny well bestowed. Caverley has bin with me and informed me off some of the particulars off that letter he last received from the honest Alderman . You must know that on Saturday I got Mr Poyen to step with our rough draught to Tom Bewick who had bin in a high wrath att us for keeping his fowl copy till Wednesday; he said it was only tricking him and delaying of time. However when I sent him ours last Saturday he was in better temper, all which I attribute to the absence off Utrecht who was gon into the country for a few days. He promised to peruse and give notice when we should have a meeting, but not the least as yet is come. I must not omit acquainting you that Tromantal called here on Tuesday as he went to visit Tom. I desired he would make this his way home and give an account if any new discovery could be made. He accordingly came and told me that all was broke off; that we had endeavoured to foist in the
Riding and Kibblesworth collieries which are neither part or parcel of Urpeth and that his brother Caverley had nothing to doe with either, and since we designed to impose upon him we should find our selves mistaken. And further he added that he did apprehend that John Ord was employed in drawing our lease, and if that was so we should never have any thing to do with the colliery. To this Tromantle replied that he knew Mr Gowland was our country attorney and that Charles Sanderson did the family's business in town, and so forth. This is the substance of what past, since which we have not had the least summons. I communicated this to Caverley who seemed surprised and would be willing to serve us to the utmost, but it is not in his power att present. He thinks the damages extravagant but att the same time joins in opinion with me that his brother will never sign unless we first comply with that and all other covenants though never so unreasonable. In short I apprehend he will raise new difficulties. It is an easy matter to find a stone to throw att a dog. We must expect all the hardships to be putt upon us, however we must dispense with them as well as we can in hopes that Caverley will be afterwards kind, and I would willingly part with Riding and Kibblesworth if Tom would sign our lease when those two are scratched out. For Mr Ord assures me that the Riding is copy hold and he thinks also that part of Kibblesworth , and as our landlord is extremely touchy we must not give him the least ground for it. Another exception he has, as Caverley told me, was that some body had wrote his brother word that you were a party concerned. To which I answered that considering the difficulties we laboured under, I thought we were much obliged to you or any body that would embark along with the Captain and me; that we needed the best off heads as well as purses. I assured him that the Captain and I proposed to have att least each 1/4; that my father had not yet fixed upon his share; sometimes he talked of having the other 1/2 for himself and the Esqire but of what signification will it be to the lessor to know what partners we admitted? I have read that part of the Captain's letter to my father ofter than once which related to the settling his demands for way leave, but never found him in an humour disposed to talk off it. You know it must come naturally and without force, therefore must wait a convenient season. Perhaps it might not doe amiss if the Captain did
write a line or two to Daniel and desire that he would put my father in mind of adjusting that matter speedily. I am heartily sorry to hear your complaints; hope that when Urpeth is once a going colliery it will afford you some diverting exercise, which may not a little contribute to the health of one of the usefullest friends in the world. I wish it may prove such, as also that this ensuing year may be successful to you without limitation. I am ... P.S. I am far from well, nay very far, yet jog on. My father is rather better than when I wrote last to the poor Captain .
61 January 24th 1712/13

Betwixt you and me, I have scarce ever bin more out of order than for these 3 weeks last past, which still hangs upon me. My complaint chiefly is off a pain between my stomach and bowels. It is constant without cease and from whence this should proceed I know not, unless it be that the humour from my legs be reverted to the stomach and so gets into my head. My appetite is so far gon that an ounce will serve me more than a day. And my head is almost constantly dizzy; this redoubles my complaints to my doctor who has altered his medicines several times without success. I leave you to judge of my circumstances, when a bottle off true and sound Newcastle clarett does not relish in the least but every glass goes against grain. I have bin vomited and purged times without number; nothing remains but patiently to submit. Sure I am that every letter I receive from you affords me more relief than the richest cordial from the apothecary's shop.

But a word of business in the next place. I am fully convinced that Headword is endeavouring all he can to undermine us; which is after so many assurances that were not extorted from him, when last in town, that he would not be concerned att present with her scarce on any terms since he had won his own colliery anew. Nay had he known that my father had any thoughts that way, he would never have interfered in the least and was sorry that by his means we were screwed up to such high terms. But I find this is all Team talk, as Kitt Stockdale phrases
it. He plays his game by Whitfield who has got the length of old Tom's foot, who has wrought him up to have a perfect aversion to us. I need not represent to you again the violent passion he was in that we did not dispatch the lease quicker. He said that was a plain indication that we did not design to take her att all, but only to prolong a treaty so as to exclude others. When we sent back his own lease with some few amendments he had 3 or 4 days to consider, after which he scratches out the most of ours and sends back word by Whitfield that if we did not comply, we should never have his consent. Then we detached Daniel who talked a little to Tom and told him there was very little difference 'tween us, that he durst affirm that if we had a meeting for one hour, matters in dispute would soon be adjusted. The next day I went to wait on him to desire he would appoint a time and place. But that very day he was taken ill and continued invisible ever since, save that Caverley had admittance once or twice and found him so ill that he durst not mention a word of business, except that he promised to send word to Caverley and us when he found himself fit for discourse. Since that he has bin removed to Kensington, and when my father very civilly sent his servant on Tuesday last to inquire after his health, the answer was that he was better but not a syllable of his hopes of seeing us shortly. This morning Caverley came here, brought no tidings from Russell Street but that his brother did recover. He seems to be very firm and steady to us. He told Mr Poyen this morning that Jack Headword should never have her as long as he lived, though he should offer never so much; that he hoped in a short time all would be concluded with us. Now my good friend time spends apace and these delays off Tom's are purely to make a hard bargain harden, thinking thereby we shall grow sick off waiting, and after all I durst venture a wager that he will not recede in the least from his demands. As to Mrs Whitfield's joining, I will be bold to say that she will never be prevailed with to doe so . If therefore there be no absolute occasion for her doing, it is better not to mention; it will raise some new scruples before the old ones are removed. For further particulars referr you to Mr Ord who knows all the objections that were last made by Tom Bewick and amendments . I must own I can but pity the circumstances of that young gentleman which seem to tend apace to ruin. I did communicate to
Daniel what you had bin doing for his service and to Mrs Smith what related to her; she wishes all lovers success. Signor is in much wrath with the fitters. Pray what steps are most advisable to be pursued in relation to Blackburn ; the Captain will inform you of a letter that my pappa Little wrote to Sir John Middleton on that head. George Vane will never let his part to any of the family. There is a share off Mrs Midford's, 1/24; I should think that Jimmy Clavering could be the best transacter there. For Tom Bewick we shall find him as averse to treat as in any former case ; could you think of any 3d person who might unsuspectedly treat with him? But can you think that any of these will be willing to part with any of their shares att a less price than they have att present? I fancy not till they have bit upon the bridle. However your thoughts are always very acceptable to ...

P.S. Pray what quantity of gallons go to a Newcastle bowl: it was inserted by Tom Bewick as 35 and 3 pints, which I altered to 35 3/4 with a reasonable streak. I am heartily concerned att your illness, which hangs long upon you. Poor Lord William Powlett sent to inquire when I had heard from his friend William , if dead or alive, for he heard not from you above a fortnight since. Besides says my lord, does he write you ever a smotty story; yes I replied. Oh then he will doe well says my lord, but why does he never write me such? I made answer that I apprehended you were in mighty favour with my lady att present and had no mind to be outed by a fat story. Oh says he, she likes it as well as I.
63 May 8th 1713

I have bin under great tribulation for several weeks by past, out off which I have no present prospect off deliverance or relief. My legs are more inflamed than off late and the same
humour has struck up into my body, stomach and head, which affects me not a little as you may imagine. My doctor has tried several new experiments by altering off his prescriptions but without the least success. All which have weakened me extremely; besides want off appetite and rest have perfectly confounded me. My wife would have the doctor sent for last night after 11 to take a perfect view off my legs, who gave me a dose off opium immediately, but alas I waked att one and never slept till 7 this morning after which I slumbered till 9. Indeed my good friend I am in a bad condition, but conceal it as much as I can from my hands to avoid trouble. Your silence has a little added to my affliction, though I partly guess att the meaning. You have taken the right method off writing to my father directly upon business, and if you don't receive an immediate and direct answer, yet now and then att some distance off time reminding him or getting Daniel to doe it will have the desired effect. I wrote to him by yesterday's post, with a desire to show you the letter; it was in the nature off a begging letter for a little off your assistance, if suited with your convenience. Must likewise desire the favour of you when att leisure to draw a short account off our partnership, that we may see how matters stand between us; and in the next place that you would lessen your stock as much as possible. I dare not venture to give you the reason att this distance, but it is what is practised by the most judicious and most substantial people off this town, and you may depend you will find your advantage in so doing. You see how I make free with my old friend, yet I have not don with my supplications. You must know that our friend Jimmy Clavering was so kind as to send me up 4 dozen off extraordinary good clarett. I got it but into my cellar on Saturday last. My father heard a character, came and tasted and highly approved, upon which could not doe less than make him a present of a dozen ; and Lord Cowper having some top company, begged a bottle of north country bear which I readily supplied him with as also half a dozen off the clarett, which was not ill bestowed. In short I am reduced to my primitive half or therabouts, therefore if you could procure me 2 dozen off that which is right good I desire you would doe it and send it per ship. Let it be entered, otherwise we shall be putt to trouble. Sometimes perhaps you may meet with a taste of good French white; there is no such thing to be had
here, none but ports. If such a thing should fall in your way, I would be very thankful for a dozen or so. Be pleased to place to my account what you disburse.

There were two complaints against one Allatson, master, who sold his coal as Bensham : the people att Gate that had some off them make a demand off praemium off my father and no such ship was reported, whence I conclude they came from our Bensham . However it would please my father much if we gave ours the name off Redhugh or any other, purely to prevent confusion at the latter end off the year. I had a letter from Daniel last post, wherein he tells me that he has or will send up our coals from Chopwell that will prove good in nature, though will perhaps be small. Pray acquaint him that for a little quantity they might be taken off, but he may depend that unless they doe come roundy we shall be dropped as heretofore. And when we were upon a project off retrieving the lost reputation off our coals, that the method is it not by sending up small coal though never so good in nature; no that will not doe. I requested him to give us a taste off the best att first that the dealers may experimentally find their amends, but now we loose time, which is very precious ... must first caution you not to show this to any. Poor Lord William has lost his only son by this lady, since which he has bin seized with a sort off an aguish fever and has bin vomited once or twice. I saw Tom Day yesterday who tells me his lordship is better. I wish you joy off our peace with France; about middle of next week we expect another day of rejoicing for that with Spain. So I hope we shall be a happy people, and remain ... P.S. I hear that the number Ten are publicly soliciting masters to load att the Grand Lease, with large assurances that they shall be delivered within 6d off Hutton and Benwell price. By this you may judge how natural it is for some people to meet with favours. Pray my humble service to honest Alderman Ramsay, whose bill of £100 I have just now paid.

P.P.S. I have just now received an account that Monsieur Bernardeau designs to import some good wine. If so it will ease you off the commission, which I discharge, as also off the white wine; but must desire you to inform yourself of himself or
Daniel and desire if they could get a piece off good white that they would order it accordingly. Adieu.
65 June 13th 1713

I had yours some time ago, for which favour I am indebted to you. Your bill was punctually paid and I have given you creditt in my account as I formerly hinted to Daniel . This sort off employ is very irksome to me on account off the bad circumstances off health and indeed my complaints increase
with the heat off the weather; however to hear off the welfare off my friends (amongst which you will give me leave to style Mr Mayor none off the least) would be a cordial and refreshment not inferior to any I receive from my doctor . Let me therefore have a line or two att a leisure minute, if such a one be to be had, for I know you have bin and I doubt are still upon double duty; I heartily wish that the same success as hitherto has attended you may accompany you to the end off the chapter. Pray let me have your thoughts a little in relation to trade; it is in great confusion beyond all dispute but as it appears to me it is not yet arrived to its full perfection. I draw my inference chiefly from the great number off large ships that are taken up by the Government att this juncture for transporting our forces from Ostend to Ireland, att least 40 sail, some say 50, which one can't expect to return into the coal trade again before September . Again, I apprehend that our oversee trade is knocked on the head, if true what I heard this day, that the French have stopped 15 off our merchant ships in Roan river; will not suffer them to unload nor return, it is supposed till such time as they know the fate off the trade bill here in England. Besides I doubt a unanimity off the number 5, who were they actually all off a piece yet I don't see how they can preserve the trade from ruin. These are melancholy circumstances, off which I can't foresee any precaution that will effect a cure. Here I conclude must acquaint my good friend that Mr Rogers and his mother have both refused absolutely to join with my father in his bill off interpleader and answer unless you be brought in as well as Trumball, which if they persist in will occasion a great delay as well as charge. Further that my father is very unwilling to comply till he had first obtained your permission. He was pleased to ask my opinion: I told him without hesitation that since it appeared to be a point off consequence, I could parole you would not oppose, nor entertain the worse thought off him for so doing. I desired he would write to the Captain to wait on you as soon as his came to hand, that you would lay your heads together, and if you had not leisure to write, that he would by the very return off the post, otherwise it will be too late. He had the account off Mr Rogers from Hebdon by last post. Now my good friend I have finished my paper, and have left room only to assure you that I am ...
66 June 20th 1713

Though I have wrote 4 letters att least to you without any answer to them, save a line or two about a month ago, yet I can't forbear you see giving the trouble of this and taking the opportunity off lamenting my misfortune off having forfeited the favour of a friend whose correspondence I so much valued; especially att a juncture when I stood most in need off his assistance and advice. You don't know in what perplexity I have bin in off late about my management or rather mismanagement of Bensham . In short I have the following account in relation to the upper seams as nicely as I could. That during my uncle Tom's life, William Johnson and Ned Carr were the acting partners for that concern, att which time those upper seams were wrought by W. Watman, Trumball and Donison, the first I was positive too; that the reserved rent was 10s per ten to the Riddells, the 10 groats to the lessees, but off any payment to either I could say nothing. That Trumball continued working for several years and does to this day, but by what authority I knew not. That some years ago when the colliery drew near Gateshead , Mr Johnson thought it for the interest off it to remove the way and lay it to the Rock steath and gives warning off the £40 lease; att the expiration off which we were disturbed by the 24. But some time after Mr William Cotesworth took a new one from the vestry off Gateshead , gave us the liberty off it and have ever since bin protected by him in the peacable enjoyment without even so much as the least acknowledgment. That about 1708 the said William Cotesworth being desirous to try his fortune in the upper seams, applied himself to Mr Rogers, one off the original partners, who told him that he should be assured off his consent but refused att first to sign his consent, by reason that he was satisfied that Henry Little and family would oppose him. Upon which the said William Cotesworth made application to Lionel Vane and the said Henry Little and obtained their approbation that the said William Cotesworth should work as Trumball had don, but upon carrying the said writing to Mr Rogers , he then recalled his promise and refused to sign. That the said William Cotesworth promised to pay the like rent etc; that I did believe
he had discharged the same yearly. Now my good friend I find that paper which we signed to you rises up in judgement against me. I should be glad off a copy; I don't remember perfectly, but as near as I can guess what we discoursed you about was an intimation to the Gateshead family that you were the person whom we approved off preferable to any, and whom we should not oppose if they let it to you, or to that effect. Now I must conjure you in the first place to secrecy, show nobody this but committ it to the flames; in the next must request off you to set me to rights if in any part I am wrong, and as speedily as you can, as also what rents you have paid, when and to whom. I again entreat you to lend me your assistance att this dead lift. I am sadly uneasy in mind, because I find it gives a friend off ours great disturbance in Red Lyon Street and the rather since a good deal lies att my door. I flatter my self with a speedy return to this, otherwise I shall look upon my self as forsaken by my old friend. Excuse this trouble att a time that I know your hands are full of business, and believe me to be ...

P.S. If you be a party in Clavering's bill, in your answer would it not be proper to own yourself tenant to the Gateshead family, as those to whom you paid rent, without mentioning the partners or any off them? Pray did you show any body that piece off paper Lionel and I signed and to whom?
67 20th November 1713

My kind friend's letter off the 15th inst came safe. I must own it was an agreeable surprise to me to find (after so many months interruption) the correspondence with my old friend revived: I read his letter over and over again, each line affording me fresh satisfaction save that which gives so sad an account of his own indisposition, which I hope att least heartily wish may be removed ere this arrive. In the mean time take a word off advice, that as this campaign has bin a long and toilsome one, those that have bin most exposed should solace themselves in their winter quarters and take care to recruit against spring. Charles Sanderson has given you an account off what passed
in Chancery att the last motion, where your adversaries were obliged, though with utmost reluctance, to comply to a trial att York. Brumell is sadly mortified and it has bin spread about att Gate that the Alderman , despairing off success in the county, was resolved to try if he could prevail with the court to remove the issue to York where he expected to find more friends in the jury; that Tom Shaftoe, being sensible off the injury he had don Sir John Clavering and Brumell , was resolved to drop his cause and give them no farther trouble; that the Alderman's aim was only to ruin poor Brumell , however that he did not despair off succeeding att long run. This is the language off the Gate, and just now one is come in who happened to be in Brummell's company last night att Billingsgate att the Tavern, where that gentleman was pretty full off liquor and declared that Mr Pitts was to putt in something into court that night which would be off singular use to his cause and he hoped would overthrow all his enemies. He entertained the dealers with a sight of a waggon way in frame, 3 yards in length, and a little waggon carrying a bushel of coals. He is att tavern all day with dealers in one room, the crimps and undertakers in another, and the 3d for masters . These leeches suck him dry and yet don't answer his ends: they demand 18d a Newcastle chaldron for what they take off, without being bound to a quantity. This perplexes him so extremely, he is weary off the town and talks off leaving it in a day or two. N. B. This minature off a waggon and the way was brought up by sea in order to have shown to the Committee (if opportunity offered) thereby demonstrating att once the excessive charge that attends coal owners, and therefore an inducement to them to grant readily a bill for settling off way leaves att a reasonable rate. This notable machine has laid concealed in a box att the Salutation ever since which is about a 12 month ago as I take it. However I shall leave that gentleman where I found him (viz.) att the Gate and proceed to the answer off yours.

What relates to Clavering Stella concern is exactly answerable to my notions. You have drawn it into a very narrow compass, into the 4 following heads: 1st either by managing the Gate, or 2dly give way to the fitters, or 3dly go on as we have don this year, or 4thly lye in for good and all. Excuse if I don't begin and say a word according to the division off my text. I begin with the last first. By lying in our rents
must sink att least 1/3d, so that we must proceed while we can but even save our selves or have but a fair prospect off so doing. The 3d point is in a great measure answered in the 4th. I doubt we have bin losers and that considerably too; besides a constant fatigue to Mr Clavering and other friends below, as well as to me above, I must needs say, such a one as I can't undergo without hazard to my life. To the 2d, one had better fall into the hands off the Devil than those off the fitters; they have scraped all the flesh off and left us to pick the bare bones. Besides when we come into their clutches we never know the expense off the trade till the year ends, and then it is too late to redress. Gift grows apace by their crafty and false representations, and still under a pretence off acting only as our neighbours doe. Which makes me call to mind when I went to school at Sir John Kayes's, we used to attend upon the warren keeper to see the diversion off cony catching. He happened to catch a couple off poll cats in his trapps one night and summons us boys to be witnesses to the execution, which was after this manner. He got a riddle, putt their tails through, after got a cloven stick and by that means pinched them cruelly; the poor creatures fell to fighting as long as they had breath, and after returned till they scratched their eyes out and att last lost their lives. Don't you think that the man who had his hand on the other side of the riddle, with his 2 sticks, was not something related to a certain generation off people who sport att the ruin off those they get their daily food by, besides what some of them horde up. Therefore I had rather throw my self into the hands off the Gate, which though they be not off the same species, yet not unlike in qualifications; with this distinction only, that they pick your pocket but they tell you before hand whereabouts the sum will be, whereas the other slides his hand into your purse, takes and takes again and yet will not bear a reprooff. I own that off 2 evils the least ought to be chose and therefore doe agree with my good friend that the first off the 4 is more preferable. But then how will this matter be compassed; not so easily as one would imagine. We have so offed cracked our words with them in relation to the quality off our coals: any time these 3 years we promised that the coals should come roundier and better than for several by past, and yet when delivered there they prove every year smaller than others, nay even to this very last voyage. Here were 9 or 10 off their ships all
in a manner together; 4 or 5 are delivered but their bulks are proving so excessively small that they have entirely ruined the markett, for the other ships off that concern that had not sold are not offered a farthing. The masters run about the Gate like so many crazed people; they bellow, swear and forswear every voyage that they will not be slaves to their fitters, that they will be damned before they will load again. Now you see in what a condition we are in. Dealers, masters and fitters are prejudiced to the utmost degree. As to the first, would you promise them 2s a chaldron if they come as they did this last year, they will not take it. Nay most off the middling dealers having burnt their fingers the beginning off the year, shun them as if infected, which will appear by the account I writ to Mr Clavering and Monsieur Poyen off what each dealer has don, and shall send the remainder now att Christmas when the whole vend will be made up. There is scarce any that could vend a quantity but Dawson, Godfrey and the 2 Oldners, and all those went to the glass houses. Now suppose we were assured off all that vend it would not amount to 5000 London chaldrons the yearly consumption, and I hear that Brummell has secured Godfrey by a praemium of no less than 12d, perhaps more, and for a good commodity which will vend it self. How can we therefore propose to doe the same by our concern, which has had the worst reputation off any that comes to markett? Jack, Mr Clavering's man, is come up to town. In case any off our ships happen to deliver this next week, I will prevail with his mistress to let him go aboard a day or more, that he may be satisfied how they work out. This boy tells me they have the roundest ship coal in the river off Tine att Clavering Stella pitts. To which I replied, Jack if you had such a stock off choice, it had not bin amiss if you had sent up 3 or 4 off the last bulks for a specimen off what they might expect the next year, but instead off that we have the worst that has come this year. What can I say to them? Or doe you think they will believe me? No, were I to confirm it even with an oath. Reputation may when once gained be easily preserved, but when that is sunk, it is nothing but length off time that can retrieve. However I will try the dealers separately (for they refuse to treat jointly with or for any concern); I will see what they say but despair off success. I could wish that Mr Clavering's (to whom I desire the contents of this may be communicated) affairs would give him leave to take a
trip up to town, that we might jointly transact what is to be done att the Gate: why might not he come and spend the holy days with us? He that is upon the spott and has seen the working off the coals, I say his words and assurances may perhaps have a greater influence on the dealers. I still continue off my old opinion, that unless the western people be not kept within bounds, that Clavering Stella is blown up and many others not a little distressed. I know it has bin proposed by Mr Pitt's agent to Roberts, who was Shallot's partner and always had his Tanfield Moor, to work 20000 chaldrons to which reply was made, then that gentleman must advance his praemium in proportion to the quantity . Brummell att the same time proposed to work at least 20000 or 25000 Newcastle chaldrons ; this last was made to several off the number ten, who were ready to engage to doe their utmost but then would have 1s 6d praemium for what ever they helped off with. In short they don't know how to ask enough. Several had the assurance to ask 1s for Main Team but nothing was complied with by either side, nor any offer made by us save 3d as usual. This is a secret and must not be disclosed. Besides they would not oblige themselves for any quantity.

My father received yours. He has had a return off his drowsiness within this week by past, which unfits him to answer yours, therefore desires you will excuse him for a post or two and the first clear day he will set about it. We have had such continual fogs as one could cut with a knife, which has affected me not a little as you may guess by this confused letter, but a word to you is enough. You have a return off my best thanks for your kind remembrance off me. Pray make my humble service acceptable to the honest Alderman , his lady and your sister Ramsay; to all I wish health and prosperity, and in a particular manner to you and yours being with all sincerity, honest William ...
68 December 29th 1713

Yours with the enclosed bill for thirty pounds came safe to hand on Christmas day. Your kind and obliging remembrance shall not be forgot, and depend upon it your health is frequently drank by your friends here when you don't think off it. Lord William never fails of doing it whenever and wherever we meet, not even excepting the College. I am sorry you give no better an account of your health ; should you drop or even if the infirmities off body should render you incapable of transacting business, from that very day should I date the declension off our trade. You are the only man that can keep the knott together, which has bin cracking a great while. Twixt us two, but let not this go any farther, I find a strong inclination in a certain gentleman to dissolve the present union, as I may so call it. I write to him this post and desired he would communicate it to you and take your advice. I likewise desired he would excuse me till the next post to you, but as I have 1/4 of an hour to the good, I thought I could not employ my self better than by a short conversation with you. I find my successor and he can't set up there horses together, neither has he any great opinion off Daniell's management; this is what I gather now and then from small and dark hints. I could heartily wish that you would let me a little into those secrets, with your remark upon them. From Daniel I have not had a line this month or more. I could freely part with 5 guineas for an evening or two with you hand to fist; I dare say that it would be off greater benefit to bodily health than all the doctor's physic for this 12 month by past, as well as an improvement to the mind. I acquainted Mr Sanderson with your commission, who said it was very well. He poor man was not so att that time having eat something the night before that did not digest, but is better since. Now my good friend my time is near expired. I hope he will excuse me if I remind him off putting the finishing stroke to his account off Clavering Stella waggon way. The particulars off wood and workmanship as I take it were formerly delivered in; what then remains but fixing a gratification answerable to the trouble you were att and the services don the concern. Make your own demands; I dare engage my word no body will gainsay
them . You can't imagine what a great sufferer I may be by the delay off our accounts not passing, and as I am informed, they can't close the year 1711 till they have that article off yours. Let me entreat you therefore to finish that offhand, by which I shall be perfectly made easy and you will thereby lay me under the greatest obligations. Adieu my good friend, let no body see this and believe me to be ...
69 January 15th 1713/4

Kind friend, I justly call you such because I frequently partake off your purse, as well as other good things. The cargo off French wine was safely laid into my cellar about a fortnight ago. That very day Lord William and Tom Day surprised my father att dinner without giving the least intimation and in the afternoon sent to me to keep them company. They then discovered the secret, which was their intention off drinking an afternoon bottle with me, which I encouraged. Accordingly they came to my house and my lord who has his eyes about him spied my cargo in the yard; began to examine what they were and whence they came, to which I gave direct answer. Oh says he, if they came from our friend William I am entitled to a bottle and one I will have. It was set upon the table and his lordship began your health the first. The whole company brought in their verdict unanimously that it was a wine off a good body and flavor but that it was not in its full perfection, being almost chilled with the cold weather, therefore advised to keep it a month att least before I went farther. You can't imagine how fond my lord was off it, insomuch that I had much ado to screen it though I gave them the very choicest off Monsieur Bernardeau's last summer's importation. This lays me under very singular obligations and what adds to them still was the passing the waggon way accounts, for it was want off that which putt a stop to our passing our accounts, at least was pretended to be such. Nay Johnson since yours wrote me word that the accounts were very backward and he did not see when yours and Mr Clavering's would be delivered in; therefore told me plainly that if his were not passed in court, he neither could nor would serve the concern longer. But this I desire may go no farther.
I have not been negligent in reminding my father frequently off Urpeth and the wayleave; nay I fail not to press him. You know his slow way off acting and indeed having multiplicity off business upon his hands, one breaking in upon another, added to his state of health, all putt together perfectly distracts him. For instance, there is an unsettled account twixt him and my uncle Robert ever since my grandfather's death, which in case off either off their demise would involve my uncle's and our family in suits and controversies without number. Mr Freak foreseeing this had 2 or 3 meetings some months since and yet not quite brought a conclusion. However in this case of ours (for so I call Urpeth etc.) I have made him sensible that since your only design in making those troublesome steps were for his and family's advantage, and how you had withstood very profitable offers which you could not well answer to your family, that he ought to declare himself openly if he would comply or att least that you should not loose the opportunity off making the best off your interest. To which he replied, you say right; I am under very great obligations to that true friend, I shall always acknowledge his favours, pray remind me from time to time, you know my infirmities, my head is seldom free an hour in a day. I have drawn out some short heads for the way leaves which I will show to Mr Sanderson and get him to digest into form. Now my good friend, since I have his leave I will pursue him close till we bring matters to a crisis. Would it not be most proper do you think, that we get the lease off the way first executed or att least ready against that off the coal lease? Depend upon it I will not be idle and from time to time you shall have an account off the success. Give me leave to rejoice with you on that this week before the Lord Chancellor Harcourt off which I doubt not you have heard by letter from Charles , whom I have not seen since, he going out of town the day after but expected back this night. I long for that long letter you promised me, which will give me insight into matters as well as persons. I am a perfect stranger to what passes with you; be therefore so free with me as to explain what and who are the chief occasions off your grievances. You may rest assured that where you enjoin a secret, it shall never be divulged to any living soul. What you think proper to be communicated to my father, let it be as it were in a letter by it self. What relates to Fenham he told me he had wrote to you about it, and ordered me to do the
like to the Captain which he leaves to yours and his transaction. I wish he would doe the like in the cases of the 2 leases to yourself and ...
P.S. My humble service to the Alderman and Mrs Ramsay .

TEI.text:
70 February 16th 1713/4
The sudden alteration off weather from one extreme to another has had a strange effect upon me. All the last week was violently afflicted with a cold rheum which fell upon my gumms and gave a sharp taste off an infirmity to which I was all along a stranger, and that was the tooth work. I got little or no rest for 4 nights successively, though made use off 2 doses off opium to procure it. Att last ventured to pull a tooth last Friday, and the day following was obliged to dine in Red Lyon Street. Got back by 6 and found my self much out off order; twixt 9 and 10 grew very bad, my tongue failed me, had no strength in my limbs, my eyes were contorted, I could scare see any body. In short it was a palsy or apoplectic fit, though not to the degree off that I had last spring. The surgeon was sent for att 11 and took away 18 or 20 ounces off blood, after which I came to my self and have bin confined to the house ever since. This day the doctor ordered me some physic and to morrow hope to make my father the first visit, though the pain and swelling in my mouth still continues. These frequent relapses prey upon my constitution much and disorders the whole fabric; I find my self considerably weakened and not capable off undergoing many such shocks, and as for business worse than ever. However as opportunity offers I am still ready to exert my self for the service of my friend. Accordingly have wrote to brother Bright to sollicitt 3 off his neighbours and acquaintance who are upon the special jury to attend the view, and my father undertakes to confirm either by this or the next post. I told him that our friends had no favour to request but that off a personal appearance, and trusted the issue to the justice off the cause. All the agents off the adverse party look with a desponding countenance; nay even their former Billingsgate advocates alter
their language, I mean the Dons. Major Loggin who has brought up a bulk off Mr Pitt's Tanfield had sold for 34s per chaldron but they soon dropped to 30, after to 29 and 28, nay I believe 27s. He has bin parcelling out near 3 weeks and was not delivered quite last night. There is but one ship off Bucks Nook. Rob Wright forced Blunkett to the tavern and engaged him to take off the bulk, some say att 28s, others say 27s, but I believe she will not be expeditiously dispatched, for there is no demand and the 11s Newcastle coals are fallen here to 25s 6d to 26, whereas had the ships forbore coming 3 weeks longer they would have met with a topping price and dispatch.
I thank you for the advice you gave in yours to Charles Sanderson . I had a letter from the north the post before I think, with an account that you had delivered in your waggonway account ; that the charge per tenn amounted to above 20s, which was thought very high considering that it was offered to be taken att 14s and that I had refused Jimmy Clavering to let him have it att 16s, thinking the latter price extravagant . Though this was not expressly mentioned yet it was referred to my memory. Your reasons off the increase off charge were added; in my answer I added another you had omitted, which was the difficulties you struggled with att your entering upon the business by the old workmen, waggon men and agents, when they did what in them lay to destroy the foundations you had laid, besides loss off timber by pilferers etc. I advised my friend to discourse over the matter with you calmly, and withal I ventured to assure him that in case any article seemed to bear hard upon us, I did not in the least doubt but you would rectify it. And further that as you were capable off serving the concern in other respects to the advantage off our pupil we might depend upon your good offices and wholesome advice. The post after I had another with account that there was £1400 due to you as balance which I must own surprised me, for according to your calculation you have not had payment for above 2 instead off 4 years. I am sure that in my hands there remains but about £700 att present, having fairly accounted to the latter end of the year 1713. Out off this I am daily paying the maintenance of the 3 misses and our pupil, besides expenses with the dealers and praemiums as they become due. I have this satisfaction that we shall have in our accounts before the Master sometime next term to the year 1714.
And as my wife could not act as guardian since her marriage, our pupil has chose and prevailed with Mr Freak to accept off that office, one who will not favour any party but push things on without delay. I must own I have not bin easy this 2 or 3 years but hope shortly shall be so. I am free and open with you. I disclose the secrets off my heart but it is to a person in whom I can confide. Therefore desire you will not take the least notice off anything herin contained but committ to the flames. I wish you a good Yorkshire journey and that it may be crowned with the desired success. My humble service to Mrs Margaret . Adieu ... P.S. I hear the last year there has bin a great demand
for English salt abroad, wheroff I hope my friend has a share. When the York assize is over and you a little recruited, should be glad to know how our joint talent improves. If I can meet a favourable opportunity shall present you with a couple off Captain Steel's last Englishmen, wherein he takes a handsome leave off his readers.

text.p: 75 April 1st 1714

I am this minute returned from the Gate, consequently you may judge not very fit for this employ, however can't omit adding a word. Charles showed me your letter off particulars what had already and what you apprehended would occur since the trial. I had an account from honest Charles Wait's mouth
off what passed 'tween the judge Robert Dormer and Sir Edward Blackett? he being then present, and his opinion was that the judge lent an ear to the baronet but could not say that he made any impression. We advised with Mr Freak on this subject (though not in time to impart for the affair would be over before a letter could reach your hand); his opinion was that none off you should appear att the sitting, so that you might avoid thereby giving the Chancellor any opportunity off soliciting a reference. However in my poor sense of matters, the course you have pursued is the best; as also engaging Berrisford and the favourite in your interest was a prudent forecast. What they are procuring by numbers off hands at Newcastle will make a noise, but from the Gate I hear not a syllable, neither doe we think it advisable to touch upon it; when we hear off their motions we must watch them narrowly. As to Coltman , he is a cunning crafty knave ; I don't say that he would not receive a sum, but att the same time underhand he would be as active as any off them in promoting any thing that had a seeming tendency off advantage to the new concern. I have ofter than once heard from good hands that he, Sir Richard , George Oldner and Blunkett were the people who have all along supplied your neighbours (though not friends) with considerable sums, with a prodigious interest; nay and that some off the above named had actually advanced them some hundreds even after the last defeat. At this rate to support the extravagancys, that mine ought to have bin a silver one instead off coal. It is absolutely carried against feeing Sir Peter, for says the Philosopher, he will not take one, but thinks it reasonable that he should be thoroughly apprised off the matter and then he will engage he will doe what service he can. And my proposal is that if we find the great Dons stirring att the Gate, we must try if we can't get the reverse with the hands off the middling ones, who are greater in numbers though not in bulk. This last is my own project. I think I have touched upon the most material points off yours. I am certain your pains are indefatigable, your judgement and management superior to any that I ever knew, and I doubt not but will be in due time crowned with success. Company is come in to see me which is not a little perplexing. Give me leave to add a word more. I design shortly to enclose for your perusal the new copy off Urpeth's lease. Suppose the Alderman has or will shortly
have the like from honest Caverley : we leave any amendments to you and the Alderman . This morning my father told me that the next month he designed for the north and that the way leave should be made easy; making use off this expression, that it was for the use and benefit off his own family chiefly and one particular friend more, by name Mr William Cotesworth which he reckoned next to his own; that it was necessary to satisfy my sister Little on that point, which he would effect the very first thing after his arrival. Adieu, Signor waits impatiently to take this to the post. I have not time to peruse what I have wrote; am sure I am to my good friend William ...

I am got abroad again after a fatiguing illness, the effects off which I find hangs upon me still, that is to say the feavor has not quite left me. I have yours to Jimmy last post, it lies before me. Don't take it amiss if I pretend to answer part off it, because that gentleman is busy taking leave off his friends. I fancy he will decamp about Monday and comes down by sea, but not a syllable must be mentioned on pain off excomunication. I have perused along with Charles Sanderson your exploits. He approves what you have don, as must all your friends; he says you and he will lay them flatt upon their backs. He wants mightily the bill off costs from below that he may get them taxed without loss of time. I can assure you our friends high and low in the House of Commons are pretty numerous, insomuch that Mr Wrightson and his party have not thought fit to make any motion as yett. As matters stand att present we don't apprehend their succeeding, though they may give us trouble enough. What you mention about certifying the stocks off coals resting att each steath att Christmas would be very useful to know. It was what I wrote to the Captain to get don above a week since, that is for Team and Bensham ; have spoke to Mr Clavering to write to Weatherly and Lowry about that of Clavering Stella . Must leave to your procuring those off Hutton and Benwell , Scotchwood and Felon , Jesmond, that off the Grand Lease if to be had, as also the prices each concern sold for, which must be returned up with convenient speed. It would be no difficult matter to prevail with the masters to certify, if occasion, that the occasion off scarcity off coals last year was soly to be attributed to the lowness of price that commodity gave att this markett the beginning off the year, which occasioned numbers off the greatest ships to seek out foreign freights. But I believe there will be no necessity for such a certificate, att least till we see farther.

Coltman, Bennett and Blunkett are the only furious advocates against the Alderman's proceedings. I believe they have most reason, being as I am informed deeply soused; the latter would not speak a word to any body att the Gate this day and is morose to a degree. But was inquiring very lately what estate Mr Wright had, where it lay and so forth, but received no
satisfactory answer. The 2 Oldners are tolerably easy and for ought I know have slipped their neck out off the halter, which perhaps was owing to a hint a friend off yours gave them 2 or 3 months since. Will Robinson be able to show his head speedily? If he did not and if the waggon carriage be in a manner excluded, then I must advise all our friends to slip no opportunity off leading down to the steaths what quantities they can possibly, so that there be no clamour for want off coals to supply the ships. John Headword seems apprehensive that his way will be pulled up and several others, but I propose that those which are not should contribute to the charge equally, being for a public advantage; and I do imagine that if this offer was made to him, it would remove his apprehensions and induce him to continue firm in the opposition. Nevill Ridly was att the Lobby the morning the petition was to be presented, but what interest he had made or who were his friends he did not impart to any off our friends. I can tell you who exerts himself against us, that is Tom Gibson, and were it not for his interest they would be able to make but an indifferent figure. I need to tell you no more off our interest with the Torys than that Lord Lansdown told an acquaintance off mine last week he was assured that if any Member in the county off Cornwall should be for the petition, he was certain they must never think of being chose again, for there they were as choice off their properties and made as much by way leaves as any people whatever. Chopwell coal is in great demand here, notwithstanding I can but join with your notion about letting if feasible, att a moderate quantity. I must leave to Jimmy to transact that matter with the gentlemen here. I long to see Frank Baker ; he was the other day to pay a visit to Red Lyon Street. Last night we melted down yours, the Captain's and Robert Ellison's tokens att Jenny Man's, where was Lord William Powlett , Charles Waite , Charles Allinson with many friends. We drank all your healths; I retired soon after ten, though some did not part till it smote little ones. Adieu. Take care off your own health, which I am sorry to find so very fickle and uncertain ...
P.S. I design when I see Frank Baker to read over Urpeth lease with him if he can spare so much time and after trust it to his conveyance to you. My father salutes you.

I begin with that part off my kind friend's letter which affects me most and putts me into the deepest concern, to have from his own hand such a melancholy account off his health. I could not rest till I had hunted out the doctor ; read him your complaints off the cough and hoarseness that stuck so close by you. To have enabled him to have made a complete prescription, he was wishing you had bin more particular in your account, but as he is no stranger to your habitt off body he has promised to send me his thoughts by this post. I spoke to the doctor about you last night in the presence off Mr Freak who has bin troubled with a cough as violent as ever I knew for several years; we thought it would have carried him off about a fortnight ago. You must know he is no friend to the apothecary's shop but leaves nature to work its own way, but att last was prevailed with to take some pills off Barbados tar, or where that is not to be had of common tar, made up after the following manner with the following powders. Take powders off ores and alicampane a like quantity, powders off liquorish double quantity. Mix them together and after roll the tar till it comes to the substance that it will make a pill. Take 10 or 12 in a day or more. It is extremely balsamic and has recovered Mr Freak to a miracle in less than a fortnight's time. He has known many others recovered by the same without any other application. He recommends it to you from his own experience. I will get some off the Barbados tar and send it you down by the first opportunity. My father had the 3 packetts from Lord William with the 6 enclosed papers; no more are since come to hand. By what I can learn we shall hear no more off the petition this sessions. It is the generally received opinion off both high and low. However it is our business not to lye dormant but be upon the guard. Charles Sanderson has attempted I believe several times to wait on Sir William Blackett? especially att the House, yet has never had the good luck to meet with him. And he must not pretend to it now because that gentleman is gon to the races att Guilford and Bansted Downs, but will do it the beginning off the week and it must be my business to remind him. I have not seen him since Monday night when he took leave off Jimmy Clavering att my father's, where were abundance off your
friends att supper, among the rest canny Frank who not knowing off this invitation came to pass the evening att my house. He and I had half an hour's discourse before we went to Red Lyon Street and are to fix an afternoon this week, when he will be free from Lord Barnard's business, when we are to solace ourselves. Jimmy went on board Mark Noble the next day but that is to be kept secret. My father sends you 6 pounds off his best chocolate by Jimmy. Your servant's which came to hand a post or two before that which lies before me now, was communicated to none but my father. The objections you made are just and would bide a strict eye to survey them. My father longs to be with you and had bin ere this had it not bin for the petition, which he can't forbear attending. We are this morning going to wait on Lord Scarborough ; if anything new occur you shall have a line.

P.S. The lord was not in town. I took that opportunity off visiting Frank Baker; had him to my self during a pipe. We discoursed on several things and he has promised to come to morrow evening to complete our conversation. Att our return we found Sir Robert Haslerigg, uncle Allanson and 2 more gentlemen that were come to dine with my father. They staid till near 8 and putt about the glass briskly. I was obliged to screen my father, so that the labouring oar fell heavy on me. I wonder Mr Poyen does not send me up the stocks att Clavering Stella : pray desire him to doe it. The 3 persons yours mention att Gate are handsomely dipped. They begin now to say that they were drawn in and exclaim against the projectors. We are all sensible that the western concerns would cut out the whole river, I mean the old standers att least, but very few off them would be able to carry on any trade to advantage. If it would not be too much trouble to you to set Thomas Gibson's case in a true light and send it to my father, he might find means to communicate it when opportunity offers. Pray excuse this imperfect answer and consider it is after a bottle and half for my share, for which I shall doe penance to morrow. I heartily wish success to the 2 doctors' prescriptions and remain ...
P.S. My father when I left him charged me to assure you off his best wishes and had not I wrote, he would; but in truth he is distracted by this afternoon's expedition.
84 June 10th 1714

I was favored with my kind friend's letter bearing date the 4th inst in its due course. It afforded me a double satisfaction, first because your complaints off bad health are not so loud as formerly and from which I am persuaded, when you have taken the Philosopher's prescription half a dozen times, you will find sensible relief and by a perseverance will entirely remove the cause. What makes me so confident in this point is that I see daily the good effects. My father began with it this week, taking 2 pills in the morning, as many after noon and the like number before he go to bed. Has found much relief as to his cough and shortness off breath. Mrs Frances Shaftoe began much about the same time, takes but half the number and yet she owns her self better by them; though I doubt she is too far gon, being inclinable to a consumption and in a manner given over by the great Rattcliff. I mention to you only these 2 instances, as an encouragement to you to proceed. The other cause off my joy is that you have so good and substantial a body off reserve in petto , wherewithal you will effectually humble the extravagant insolence off your antagonists. I can assure you they don't in the least suspect any after-game. They sleep secure without either watch or ward. This I could discover by Blunkett and some other the great Dons, who with a smiling countenance asked me yesterday att the Gate if Bucks Nook led any coals. I replied, if they consulted their own letters they were able to answer the question themselves; that I did never correspond with any off the proprietors or agents off that concern. Oh, says Blunkett , but we hear that they are still pulling up the way which lies in a lane, a known reputed high way; that these practices were executed by a Lady Hutton as they were informed. However to prevent that they were forced to keep an armed patroll by night for 3 miles together etc., a vast charge and what
poor Brummell could never bear. No, I answered, without he calls in aid some off their body, who were always ready to assist the distressed and so forth; thus we bantered till after one a clock.

But I must now proceed by taking leave off those master pieces off impudence, and acquaint you that you mistook a great toe for a least. My father is well off that ailment but has had a strange hoarseness or sinking off his voice ever since Saturday, and even off that he is much better and hopes to complete by lying in the air for a fortnight; to that end has secured a lodging att Kensington, where I fancy he designs to morrow. He would not divulge a syllable off what our trusty friend communicated till I had obtained his leave for so doing and for the reasons which he will communicate. I was assured and can depend that it will be kept a secret. Perhaps some things may fall in naturally in way off discourse which may give an insight, though but a short one, and may give a handle to an enquiry. If I find my self out off order I complain, but to whom should I? Why to my friend. But as it is not in his power to relieve, ought not he go to the best off advice and give some hints off my distemper that may lead the doctor to a distant knowledge off my symptoms; who without making any discovery may point out something that may be off present service and prevent for the future. A word to the wise. Trusty Frank left us last Monday noon, taking his rout by Oxford so that when he can reach Mr Mayor I know not. After my prescriptions for your health, my father recommends to your particular care not to travel late att night and never without some person; and sent you by our friend his own pair off pocket pistols, which he presents you with but at the same time enjoins you never to travel without them. They are clever, well made and lye in little room. I just long to hear how you will mumble poor Billy. When I mention that name it puts me in mind off our accounts. I wrote to Jimmy as formerly hinted: he took Peter to task, who has promised a care more than ordinary but that shall not doe. I will attack him likewise, for if he keeps him he shall not entrust him with a sight off our books, but twixt you and me Jimmy is more suspicious off another under his roof viz. Daniel Poyen . Don't take the least notice. That concern is under most unhappy circumstances considering the present situation. The differences twixt poor
Jimmy and John Johnson grow daily to a greater height, which must undoubtedly be a vast prejudice to that concern, which without them is under the greatest difficulties. This makes me frequently think off resigning and I believe shall speedily doe it. The Bishop of Durham was to go out off town this day. He generally talks off giving my father the trouble of a trial about the eastern fell but I don't hear he took notice off it yesterday when my father took leave off him. If you hear off any stirridge off that sort, you will be so kind as to impart to ...
92 London October 26th 1714

After having been passed from constable to constable for about a fortnight, without much fatigue, we arrived att this place off Saturday night, where we design to take up our winter quarters. I find that as the town off Whickam in situation is much exalted above the rest off its neighbourhood, so does its zeal for the present establishment exceed in lustre. Pray remember me kindly to those true patriots, Canny Frank and the honest greeve, and that jolly blade who threw the priest's wife's mug into the fire (though unknown) should not be forgot. It is a pity there were not more off such public spirits
dispersed over your diocese. Mr Wright got to town 2 or 3 days before us; was att the Gate on Friday or Saturday and assured the dealers that Bucksnook would after all revive, seemingly intimating as if the Alderman and he had come to terms and he hoped this next year to clear all their old demands. In short I am still off the same opinion, that it is better to end this dispute upon reasonable terms than run the hazard off a tedious contest, the determination off which must be owned uncertain. Especially considering the unsettled situation off public affairs att present and a medley it will be att best. His Majesty is off an admirable disposition, willing to doe every thing for the best. Here are great numbers off laden ships come into the river, I believe the whole fleet that was loading att Newcastle when I was there. No demand, so that the price is very low, which must occasion complaints both by masters and dealers where there is no just occasion. My uncle is just come thence; he tells me off some against our Stella and they needs will have it that your coals are mixed with them, which makes the alteration. I ridiculed that wild notion as I shall doe it in person att the Gate on Thursday next. I know not but that I must trouble you with an enclosed list off the justices for our county as they stood this present year; if you know any that are fit to be added, let me know. The method this Chancellor takes in adding new ones is if they be qualified with a brace off hundreds a year; I do believe there are many in the present list that will fall short. Pray how does our Farnacres drift go on? You will make an offer of my best services acceptable to our worthy landlord off Westgate Ramsay , to Mrs Margaret and all friends. Adieu, I wish you all health and happiness, and rest ... P.S I am sorry that Jackson should have come as a deputy to the controllers. I can assure you my friends have not bin awanting in their application, not for that post but some other off consequence; no success as yet but not without hopes. I charge you not to mention a syllable. I must have a speedy answer to the enclosed. My father salutes you. Just now I hear the King , who has bin mightily pressed by a very great man who solicited for his friend a military preferment , took courage and told him, my lord, I have gratified you in all your
demands but am resolved in this to oblige another. If you will not, I will make my self easy. Upon which the lord retired into the country.
102 February 17th 1714/5

Doubtless after my last which carried Sunderland measure, you will admire att my impertinence in troubling you so soon again. The principal reason is that you would get the enclosed conveyed safe as directed and speedily, and the next is to salute you with a paper called the Citizens' Advice to their Representatives in Parliament if I can get one; if I should fail you will see them att large in this day's Flying Post. They will please Mr Mayor's taste to a nicety, though not your brother on the north off your river. Perhaps you may hear that Ross, Ecklin and Hill are to keep their regiments ; they have made their submission, it is probable, and his Majesty as he is wondrous good is pleased to continue them. I designed a visit to Lady Bows and son yesterday with
an intention to touch a little upon the borders off her ladyship's concern att Hutton but both off them were so ill off colds that I had no admittance. Tried again this day but they were gon down to Westminster , I suppose to see Captain Byron. Indeed the young gentleman I am afraid is in a very bad way; he has had a violent cough accompanied with an hoarseness that has hung upon him ever since he came to town. Would not listen to any advice, trusting to the strenght of his constitution that nature would work it off, but within a week he found himself obliged to send for a doctor; I wish he may not have future cause off repenting the delay. Last night I paid Mr Freak within a very few pounds off the second thousand, so that he has had in all off me upwards off £2030 which he has laid out in classis orders for the benefit off the Infant. I have a bill on Tom York for £49 1s which I expect to receive on Monday next out off which I shall pay your bill to Mr Cay's order, and you may draw on me att sight any time next week for £100 to Charles Sanderson. Att the same time if you give another on the account off balance off my own account, I can give my self creditt for it and then I can give in a clear account to the Master; I call it clear, because I shall not have a five penny piece in my hands off the executorship money, and that I would willingly doe that the court may see I have given a full account of what I was entrusted with. Indeed my good friend if Dan charges more than 5s for the pan coal, I think he bears hard on you. If have time shall write to him this post on that subject and answer his last. He has to my thinking strange notions off the London trade; has given his opinion to lay aside the dealers entirely, to allow the masters 2s per Newcastle chalder and let them fight their way, by which means he proposes cutting off all charges off management here. I question much if that be complied with, if it obtain the desired end. Sure I am it will be the worst off presidents that ever was brought on the trade. Will make all concerns very touchy and uneasy; this makes me remind you to see if she could be let and then the undertaker or undertakers may menage as they think fit. I frankly declare to you that those coals as they came up the 2 last voyages were as much sought after as any att Gate, always fetched within 3d off Main Team and frequently equal price. I could say more on this head but will only mention this: that Blunkett, Watts,
Coltman, Bennett, when I paid them the praemium at Christmas which was 6d per London chaldron , told me that if they had suspected I would have paid them as I did, that concern instead off vending 17000 London chaldrons should have sold 40000, and upbraided the 2 Oldners and Godfrey for not letting them into the secret. This is enough to say so I shall close all with assuring that I am ...

I am not neither have I bin these ten days in tolerable plight off health, which made me answer yours by piecemeal; sometimes I recommended half a dozen lines to the Colonel to communicate to you, att others to Daniel or Peter, as opportunity offered. I don't remember to have omitted any thing material; if I have you must attribute it to bodily infirmities. Pray what are your thoughts off my amendments to the Chopwell scheme formerly sent up signed by Dan, Peter and Weatherly? I must own I wish that concern were let for the term off 3 or 4 years and then I should be eased of a perplexing and daily trouble. Ever since Wedensday we have bin alarmed
with the loss of the new ship called the Clavering and yesterday it came confirmed both by land and sea. What I mention this for is upon the account off the 3 misses off that name who are great sufferers thereby, having all the household goods etc. that were left to them by their mother in that bottom, besides all the family pictures, which can never be retrieved. Poor Dick Bellassis is computed to have lost near upon £1000, he having 1/8 off the ship, all his house furniture and some say a good deal off plate and some jewels on board. I am now preparing to go along with our pupil to the Master in Chancery with our books off accounts for the year 1713, as also to get his receipt in form for the last thousand pound I paid into court, which probably a certain gentleman now on the road may be so curious as to desire a sight off.
