Poor man, I dread his coming up for his own sake; if he be not provided with a very considerable sum towards the discharging a good part off his balance, I don't know the consequence that will ensue unavoidably. The court has had hitherto a more than ordinary complaisance upon his account, but if there be but a weak performance off what has bin so long promised, I doubt his reception will not be what he expects. But don't let this go further. The church has lost the greatest pillar and ornament in the person off the much respected Bishop off Salisbury who I hear is to be succeeded by the honest Bishop off Oxford and his post to be supplied by Dr Potter, Archbishop Thom Tenison's chaplain, to the great mortification off high church . I enclose you the Dutch ambassador's speech to his Majesty which you will not grudge reading, and let Mrs Margaret have the perusal of it. I can't but apprehend a very bad coal trade this year. Our joint adventure in Farnacres I wish may answer our expectation; hitherto we have had but a sour and expensive prospect. P.S. The enclosed from Denzill Onslow came to hand this afternoon and he himself followed a few hours after. Has promised to let me have a particular off the last contract on Monday next, which shall be sent you, as also will befriend you as much as in the power off a commissioner . As to your adventure off dails, I have informed my self particularly off one who has bin on the same foot with you but happened to be in 3 or 4 cargoes. His advice is by sad experience
to sit down with the first loss. The Colonel has a discretionary power for both parties here concerned to act what he thinks most beneficial in relation to Elswick . I must add no more than that I am on all occasions ...
114 6th October 1715

Your two last came safe and bring a most particular account off transactions in your parts. I do assure you they were very kindly received and laid before the Secretaries by your friend off Bedford Row. They are much obliged to you for their intelligence and never see him but are inquisitive
what news he has from your country, for as much as I can gather they depend more upon you than all the rest. Before I proceed must take notice that I have (pursuant to your orders) bin att the Grecian to see Mr Gibson. It was as rainy an evening as any we had this year. Not one off the family was there; which gave me an opportunity off transcribing that part off yours and sending it the next morning by express. This afternoon your above friend came to see me almost half drowned; tells me he has several commissions from the two Secretaries. 1st. They desire you will inform them if T. Forster be gon over to Lord Mar. Also that there are some English gentlemen gon lately northwards in their way to that lord as is supposed; if possible to learn their names. Pray who is the receiver general of your customs? 2ndly. They will have from you the state off Northumberland with your opinion what force would be necessary to prevent any disturbance in that or your county, as also what would be requisite to secure the peace off your corporation. 3dly. You are further requested to send your thoughts freely, and that what relates to public business might be in a paper by it self that it may be kept by them to refresh their memory. And lastly I am ordered to assure you from the above mentioned parties that if any thing be to be don in relation to the troops, send word in time by making any offer and it will be complied with. I am charged not to read yours to any one body. They caution you to take what care you can that your letters be not opened to the northwards. I have no reason to suspect as yet any practice off that sort; therefore you will direct as usual. I could wish to have a further account off parson Cuthbert Fenwick off Morpeth I think; the Captain writes word that Sir John Delaval gives him the character off a Tory. This should be sent by the first post (though I doubt it will be too late). The Duke Somerset and Lord Castlecomer espouses him strenuously for Long Horseley. I doe what I can for parson Cowper, but am not so sanguine off success as formerly because his grace is not to be putt out off humour att this time off day. There will be 6000 men from Flanders speedily. Exert yourselvs and all will go well, and no encouragement will be awanting. This is the last push off the desperate faction, which I hope when once over will settle us upon a solid foundation. Now dear friend excuse hast and believe me to be ...
122 1 November 1715

I am in concern that you should be deprived off the use off your pen, though you are so generous as to supply that defect by your deputy. Your intelligence is so much in vogue that no sooner is the post come but I have great men's valets waiting for the produce off your packet. However I can assure you it is not to above two that I will trust them out off my hands; and it is a high favour don to those I read them too and those are very few in number. My good kinsman ever since my father came to town, as I formerly hinted, is not so zealous; he is att present a housekeeper by reason off a sore throat, but he fails not once off seeing your dispatches. Herafter I shall make use off another hand. This morning my father and self went to Duke off Devonshire to impart but he was not to be seen; thence to Mr Walpole who was not to be met with; we took Lord Somers in our return and were there also disappointed. I do imagine they were all sommond to Council. So we lost our labour. Pray send me the present supervisor's name, as also that off the person you would have succeed him. I will not let my friends rest from soliciting. Is he supervisor for our county or only our ward? Pray continue your early accounts. Our friend in the Fields has bin ill off the strangury for several days but after the post came he found him self easier, which I attribute to the good account yours brought, though is not so well this day. But don't take the least notice off his health in your return. The parson recommended by Alderman White, Matthew Foster, your Colonel and other friends has succeeded att last for Long Horseley, notwithstanding as I hear your magistrates joined in a recommendation on behalf off Willcox, Sir John Clavering's chaplain, which makes the obligation the greater. Att the Grecian the talk is that the Dutch forces would be embarked last Sunday, so that now they wait only the wind. The cantoning your troops as proposed, is looked upon as the produce off a solid judgement . A report is current that James Butler did putt to sea ten days ago from Ambleteux not far from Calais and is said is returned back to France, finding his scheme in the west was broke. Others will have that a man off war gave chase to his ship, which obliged him to return; but of either off these reports I can't depend as what comes from the
north. When things come to calm and these burlys are over, you may assure your self a lasting security may be reasonably expected. I am summoned to attend Mr Freak and am obliged to deliver up my arms, my pen and ink, and rest to my father. Both off them are much att your service and so is ...
127 19th November 1715

Honest and trusty Will, your last was by mistake delivered to my father which I retrieved this afternoon, when he was looking for the chapter in Ezekiell. Within the liberties off Westminster the justices have begun with their convictions by order off Counsel and had delivered in their rolls to the clark off the peace, where it has laid sometime. An enquiry was made by the Counsel what was don by the justices and on Monday I think they design to make their representation. In Essex they began earlier, so that it is hoped these presidents will spread all over the nation. I remember my father as he read over yours, when he came to the particular off the caveat, said that was done. As to James Crags and your assistant, I must referr to my Lord William who is very active and ready to serve his friends. Sir Walter Young is but slow. But indeed the confusion the whole ministry and nation has bin in makes that they can't lend an ear, or if they doe it is in att one and out off the other; but now it is hoped this hurricane is over, and shortly we expect a calm and from thence that recommending a fit person to serve will be listened unto. What you propose about the militia would be of singular use att this time; they could not fail off picking up abundance off strollers, which though no corporal punishment were inflicted on them, yet were they but marked so as to be known, a watchful eye might be set on them against another time. One would think that your Lord Scarborough and Mr Carr could not but see the necessity off doing it and off what service it would be. This account off the battle twixt Argyle and Mar is the confused'st account sure ever was given. It sinks our joy conceived on the first report. Pray can you reconcile what became off the centre off our army? Had the first report we had come confirmed, you would have had South Sea att near par this day and others in proportion. Sure I am my friend had not so much as a finger in that narrative. Will, I just long for a better account from those parts. The officers here, not one off them can reconcile it, nay
even his grace's best friends. Adieu, it is past 8; pardon me for I am ...
129 1st December 1715

Methinks tic a long time since I heard from Mr Mayor which makes me apprehend now that he has less troublesome business on his hands, that he is more sensibly affected with the late prodigious fatigues he underwent; too heavy a burden fell to his share, I am satisfied a greater than any one pair off shoulders could bear. I hope my last with an enclosed to Peter came safe. Upon the oath taken by Spearman that he was worth £20000 beyond all just demands on him, the statute formerly mentioned was suspended. However by this his creditors will have a fair pull att him if they menage right. I am desired by Bartholomew Scott to know what steps you have taken towards the recovery off the £50 bill I formerly sent you. He desires you would show him no favour and sends me word that the rest of number ten have had a meeting this week and are resolved to prosecute him for the money due to them, which is to a considerable value. Your country general with the chief off the North British Preston prisoners are to be brought to town to morrow. The inferior are distributed in several off the county goals below. I can tell you for certain that this day Mr Masterman, father to the young gentleman off that name whom you know, is appointed to go down to Lancashire and take informations, not only against those that were actually in arms but all who were any ways concerned in aiding and assisting the rebels. On these informations the Attorney General is to frame his prosecutions. He received his credentials and instructions with recommendations to several well wishers in the country this morning and sets out this afternoon. This gentleman is very capable and zealous. There lye now att the Tower wharf six vessels from 100 to 200 ton each, on board which are to be embarked many pieces off heavy canon, 20 cohort mortars and 4 others off the largest size, proportionable ammunition off all sorts for Edinbrugh . I hope soon after this you will see the van off the Dutch that marched hence beginning off last week. You will find Bucksnook in the utmost distress next year, they have not a friend att Gate will trust them a half penny piece. They will suffer unpitied. Adieu honest Will, take care off your health, in doing which you will oblige the public as well as ...
P.S. We were yesterday to visit our Lord Lieutenant but he was abroad; we see his son but other company being with him we had no private confabulation.
132 Tuesday near 10 att night

I have bin obliged to attend our board all this day and a new commissioner off our office, who invited us to dinner and with him we have bin ever since. However I can't omit adding a few friends to my good friend. You must know that I am much out off constitution, upon certain intelligence that the Colonel had not appeared so zealous upon the late disturbances as could be expected, nor my father's friends, by which it plainly appears that a certain gentleman would make his interest att court by taking all upon himself. He talks much off his indefatigable pains, such as his lying whole nights att the gates off the town ready to receive expresses as they came from this town, and giving dispatchs to the scouts he sent out whenever they returned, with much more off this nature to ingratiate himself. This a friend off ours had from a friend who heard it told to the Prince himself. This you may imagine has not a little discomposed our old gentleman after the hazard the Colonel run and his friends, besides the expensive part, that they should be reputed rather as indolent and inactive att that time off day. Poor Lord Scarborough I dare say had not the least hand in this misrepresentation for he has bin in Sussex almost ever since his coming from your parts and is there yet. My father is very inquisitive after the full particulars, which as soon as come to hand shall be communicated att large. This morning Lord Lumley came and made a visit to my father. He expressed himself very frankly upon the matters of the north; told us that the saving off the town att first was in the greatest measure owing to the Colonel and your self, who by means off the friends off your county kept the town quiet, and expressed himself very handsomely upon that occasion. By which I perceive from what quiver the malicious arrow was shot. I read him part of your 2 letters; he desired me to draw an abstract and send him, and he would take care that your desires be answered by laying before Lord Townsend etc. He says he will make some off your Newcastle people smart; he is very zealous, nay I may say extraordinary, from whence I expect something will be don. You would doe well to write to cousin Little and Mr Gibson upon the subject you mention for they may be both serviceable. I can't
omit mentioning one passage that happened between a gentleman of my acquaintance and another of yours and mine. Talking off the affairs off the north, he showed him several informations that he procured, among which was that against George Baker? . My friend was curious to see it but he told him that it contained nothing material and so took it out off his hand. From this I conjecture many will be sunk, which is an abominable practice. I shall make the best use off your letters I can by imparting them to some I hope one time or other will make inquiry after such practices. I have not had time to consult a method for correcting the abuse committed by your being putt to the charge off shamm scoundrel packetts, but from those I have talked with their opinion is that you should seal them and return to the Post Office, who will be obliged to return you the charge. Lord Lumly was inquisitive if any officers either custom house or excise were not zealous for the Government , that Mr Walpole had desired to be acquainted with them and he would take care to set those matters right. Do you think if you wrote a letter to him on this subject, I dare say it would be the most effectual method of having redress. Excuse this scrawl for I am above half seas over ...
139 25th January 1715/6

I am indicted to two off yours off no small size each, but how to discharge is the difficulty. We have had a cold sort off a thaw, which does affect me cruelly. There is no stirring abroad neither in coach, chair nor foot without manifest hazard off breaking bones, so that we are all in a great measure confined to our respective habitations; from whence you will conjecture that one has nothing to doe but answer letters, but that is not my case for I am in pain from head to foot, sick att stomach and so listless that I am not master off one clear thought, consequently fitter for bed. However before I go there will attempt to answer as far as I can your favours. Your town was unworthy off so honest a man as Jurin; as you very well remark, posterity will have reason to curse those who have had any hand in making him uneasy in the post he was possessed off. But what other can be expected from such a set off governors ? And to be succeeded by such a wretch, who is not worthy off wiping his shoes, is no less admirable. By this they seem resolved that the
next generation shall continue in the same obscurity. Ignorance is the mother off devotion. Oh blessed mother church! You have named the person that poisons all and yet I wish he can be outed. Mr Freak spoke to Lord Somers about it but his bodily informitys disable him prodigiously from doing service to his country as well as particular friends. As to the forfeitures, you need not doubt they will be punctually and rightly applied. Charles Sanderson you have described to the life. I have pressed him by letter as well as word off mouth to send a petition drawn to the High Sheriff ; he pleads multiplicity off business in excuse and promises fair. Honest Gilbert Spearman is as great a master in his way as Edward Montagu? was in his, with this distinction that the first does it without mask, the other picks your pocket and att the same time smiles in your face. Pray push what you can to get in that bill; if money be not to be had, had you not best return the bill to Scott? You know how I am circumstantiated in Clavering Stella . The season for opening the trade is att hand and to be att an uncertainty att this time off day may prove off the worst consequence. I hope here this arrive that the gentlemen have come to a determination one way or other, for till I hear that would not exchange a word with the dealers. I am fully convinced that all your affairs have suffered much by your London journey and especially the vend off your coals. I should have thought the Gentlemen whom you were serving obliged to have lent you an assisting hand but when the business is over and done the benefactor is generally forgot. This is the way off the world. Your Chester friend shows himself every day more and more in another interest. The baronet has kissed the hand, but you may rest assured that if any thing can be made out against him he will not escape. This I had from undeniable authority.

I come in the next place to your bill in Chancery which bears date the 20th. I doubt you are too true a prophet concerning the regiment . I have frequently showed that part off your letter dated the 2nd December where you pointed out correctly what has since happened in relation to that gentleman . Our divisions att home have given him encouragement . The Government has had a watchful eye upon him. We have a fleet att sea or just ready, about ... sail, I can't say in a body as yet but you will hear off them
shortly. I am off your opinion that the cruisers have not bin so diligent in their station as could be expected. We long to hear off the march off our army towards Perth, which if it please God to prosper with success will be a vast strengthening off the King's friends. If Sir Charles Hotham does not represent effectually the usage some off his men have met with he does not doe justice, but as he is a man off mettle and honourable I doubt not in the least his seeing them righted. As to the blew coat excise man, I have bin speaking till I am weary. Lately I discoursed Roger Gale about him. Says he Mr Carr should doe that, I am a stranger to that town and a young commissioner ; however if you would send him an information, he would out him in spite off William Carr . Had not that gentleman this man represented to him among many others? But he is a slippery spark; my father has not bin able to find out to the bottom off what he went in search off. As to the victualling and clothing contracts , it is my admiration what interest those gentlemen have to succeed in it. By what underhand means they work. As I take it those undertakers are generally recommended to the commissioners by the Treasury, where I have not the least interest, having bin soliciting augmentation off salary as all in that office have had save another and my self, but without success. I delivered yours about Breaks in favour off Edward Mawson to Sir Richard Sandford last Saturday and gave him liberty to make use off my fathers and my name. He did it att the House that very day to Mr Walpole, had his promise it should be done. They are so overcharged with business that none can get a minute's discourse with them but some that are their intimates. I doe my best towards improving your frequent advises to the public benefit but am much concerned that my endeavours prove off no greater use: your indefatigable pains and zeal is as good as thrown away. It happens that those people who ought to inform themselves of what passes I am a stranger too, and am apt to believe that they take all their representations from Lord Scarborough's William Carr . Were you not amazed to see in the Gazette that Lord Scarborough had delivered the address introduced by the former. I abstracted part off your letter wherein you pray that it be discountenanced; left it with Lord Lumley who promised his assistance and that he would remind his father. Not above ten days ago my father and self waited on the Lord
Lieutenant , brought that subject upon the board, told him it was an affront to his lordship that they would not accept off the association he left them; but you see to what purpose. This makes me wary off transacting matters with people that blow hot and cold. But poor man he is directed by another person who never plaid a game but fast and loose. My father went this morning to the Lords to talk about the armies but came too late. Last post I see a letter from Leverpole with account that young Pearson has bin wrought upon by a sister who is with him to confess and has swore to as well as signed the information. Since that is, I believe they will be very nice off sending a copy (least it should miscarry) till after the trials. However I will attempt it. I design showing the latter part off yours about the suspension of habeus corpus to some friends off the House. I am perfectly jaded so fit to take a nap. 26th January : this morning att 11 I was saluted by your last; have imparted what is most material to a particular friend, from whom I expect benefit. Adieu ...
P.S. There is a flying report that to the west our men off war had taken 2 ships loaded with arms.
145 4th April 1716

I am so taken up with phisicking night and day that I have not so much as a moment's leisure to think off business. This instant I am so grip'd that my face is enough to sower a barrel off bear,
so that I don't know how to set about answering either off yours. Accept off thanks in the first place for both your favours. The proposed way cross Darwent I looked upon as next to impracticable, if it were only the difficulty off securing it against sudden floods. I can't pretend to judge off it, having only a distant idea off the situation; however by your prudent forecast in securing Anderson's and Thornley interests you have so cast their bowl off its bias that there is no prospect off its ever coming near the jack. I concluded that Silvertopp had bin so engaged with his friends in October last that he would not have bin able to show his head, but he is a cunning, crafty blade. Lady Bows though a timorous woman, yet will not part with a penny to any friend unless she have att least its worth. Old Wortley perfectly distracts her; she gives out that he is actually working 8 off her pitts in the broken mine, that he will not suffer her agent to view, that he will certainly thrust her to the vengeance. She adds that he and John Ord are two off the greatest rogues that ever a county was blessed withal; they will by right or wrong come att means to purchase estates, but att last must go to the Devi l. I presume the new invention you went to see is designed to be fixed above Ironside's house in the wood. The Colonel writes me word that they had sunk about 8 fathom below the main coal att Farnacres and 2 fathoms att another pitt. He owns she is troublesome and expensive, but att this rate we shall loose this year before we get a pitt coal'd. Why don't we fall upon the Alderman's liberty (who I rejoice is better)? The main coal must be drained there I should think, as much as ever will be. When I am engaged I don't love to sit still. Tic above 3 weeks that I wrote to Peter for closing his books this year to clap the £260 to Coal Chamber account, which we hope sooner or later will be reimbursed. I had a letter last Monday from Daniel ; he is sadly in the miff and hup't. He wishes he had never engaged in the matter. I am sure to have my head in my hand if this bargain miscarry. Mr Freak never sees the post but inquires if an end be not putt to the lease. Therefore must beg off you to lend your assistance in forwarding. I write to Dan this post and encourage him. I tell him that John Bullock is the man I propose to take a view every 14 days in the Infant's behalf, that the charge may be 5
or 6 guineas ; that if Weatherly would take a moderate salary as steward I thought it might not do amiss. He is used to the tenants , knows perfectly what allowances and bargains were made with the tenants etc. and what were the terms to be performed. If £10 or 12 would doe, he might deserve that. There is a good deal off writing etc. As to a general liberty to the alderman off leading any coals, I never did consent but for leading down that pitt which was led from the Grand Lease and those from Hedley Fell, provided our tenants were to be employed in the same, and no farther. I read the alderman's letter to my father and Mr Freak as also Daniell's; they both did agree that such a liberty might enable the lessee to make our Chopwell reputation and the better to perform his bargain. Upon this the Guardian ordered me to write to the alderman and Daniel to that purpose, but they are to be restrained from the use off the way for any other coals, save as above.

When the new act comes into the house, Mr Freak will discourse and inform his friends with the real design and I hope some way or other to get Mr Gibson possessed. My Lord William has appointed a day every week for several by past to wait on Mr Walpole by this gentleman's own appointment . When we came, the day was putt off till that day 7 night, and so from time to time till he kept his bed and I am afraid will never get abroad again. If he doe he shall see your enclosed; if not one off the Secretaries shall, though I wish to better effect. Dear friend had I had yours before had given an answer to the alderman , your sense off the matter would have influenced me. But after having given the word, honour does oblige, though it does not a certain lady with whom you have a contest. I don't see that we shall be thanked scare for all our pains and endeavours to preserve this scurvy trade and that is but sorry wages. Adieu honest Will, let me beg off you to dispatch this lease for I shall be teased to death by the Guardian till it be don ...
148 10th May 1716 past 12

Yesterday was the first day I got into the Fields for a mouthful off fresh air since Tom Shafto and I walked in Kensington Gardens. I have struggled with a stout feavor ever since which still hangs upon me. I was in hopes had got the better off it but last night I did not get 2 hours sleep, and this minute the doctor is come to visit and ordered me to swallow a dose off opium, which is don. I am extremely faint in spirit, swett vastly and in short almost dissolved. This made me lay hold off the opportunity (though my letter does not go till to morrow) least I should be disabled then, to return you my best thanks for your last as well as former favours , which must be ever acknowledged with a grateful sense. Yesterday was the first time I set pen to paper, when I wrote to honest Peter and enclosed him Mr James Clavering's bill on you for £50 payable ten days after sight. It has laid by me ever since I have bin ill. I desired him to discount it with you on account off waggon way. Daniel is much in the miff and desires to be excused from acting further in the affair of the view off the
way. This made me desire Peter that he would wait on the Colonel some day att your house, and I did not doubt but your 3 heads would be able to putt that matter upon a sure foot. He will read you what I wrote. I earnestly covett to see an end made; Mr Freak presses upon me why I don't execute the lease. What I wrote to Daniel related to a former I wrote him a month ago att least, wherein I encouraged him to proceed; that as the alderman was obliged to leave the way in every respect as he finds it, what had his new undertakers to apprehend if they did perform their part? If they did not design to doe it, we must come upon the lessee and he upon them. I shall be glad to hear from you. Your lines revive me much; are much more so than a cordial blister, to use the doctor's words, that Wakelin clapped on my back a foot square. I leave this open till to morrow, when you shall hear further how it fares with ...

P.S. What tidings from Farnacres? Is any good to be expected; if there be I shall be agreeably balked. Adieu. 11th: I have had but another scurvy night. The feavor lies in my head and stomach and a load on my spirits. The doctor talks off sending me to Hampstead for the air. I have bought a horse att Smithfield att the doctor's pressing instance, which cost me £25. I don't approve of him, he trots hard and a very plain nag.
152 26th June 1716

I rode out off town yesterday about half a dozen miles and dined with our friend Mr Tomson, and in the evening att my return was welcomed home by yours, which came safe and brings Scott's bill; which I was glad to see for that fellow made such a noise and complaint ffor want off it as was not to be endured. The mistake off calling it a £50 bill was soly mine. I doe assure you Mr Walpole is no stranger to your recommendation. I had employed several off my friends, att
certain distance off time, to lay before him Ned Mawson's case; nay even since his last illness got cousin Honywood to remind him, but these great men will bide teasing. However this your last supplication by Lord William I hope may prove more effectual. My father and I design waiting on his lordship to morrow where ten to one he shows me your original. I shall perhaps see Sir Walter Young this afternoon and shall speak to him as you desire about Selby. This knight's son is upon the point off committing matrimony with a niece off Sir Gilbert Heathcote's. The information I gave you was as I had it but since have had a more certain account; therefore you will correct it and read George Pitt instead off Lady Clavering . What relates to colliery, I mean the bringing to reason the great man, deserves a due consideration; and as my father and uncle are partners it will require a joint meeting, which I shall take care off before the first leaves the town and I shall putt them both upon speaking their minds freely and openly. Your opinion off Felon and the Park, and the ability off the water catchers to perform what they undertake, is my sheet anchor in the coal trade and on what I soly depend, as also on Whickham upper seams off which I all along entertained a favourable opinion; but as to Farnacres I never could, and have not as yet any reason to alter my first conception. I have seen Sir Walter and took notice off what you recommended; he assured me it should be done. I showed likewise our friend Roger the copy off yours to Lord William ; his advice was to lay it before the Board off Treasury, Mr Walpole being taken ill off his old distemper the stone. While I was discoursing that gentleman att the Grecian, in came Lord William who immediately took out yours which I read without taking any notice. He was att a loss what to doe. I proposed laying it before the board, which he seemed to acquiesce in and promised to doe it. There it was I met with the captain's son off Hexham, who received a letter from Newcastle with an account off John Bell's death; this was so remarkable a piece that I believe if true you had not omitted it. I have made your compliment to Sir John Colebatch who received it very kindly and desired to return his best thanks. The Parliament is prorogued this day to the 7th August next. His Majesty I believe will set out next Thursday for Holland ...
P.S. I don't know if the Captain had got any Lisbon wine or if he had only the prospect off getting.
157 East Street, 2d October 1716

For this fortnight or longer I have bin extremely bad; a constant dizziness in my head, sick att stomach and am apprehensive off a touch off the palsy, being held much after the same manner I was 3 years ago. This makes me wish Sir John Colebatch's return. The other day I took away 21 ounces; the blood had not bin out off the vein 2 minutes till it turned all blew and yellow. I took here picra every day but gave no relief. Yesterday T. Wakelin sent me a potion which had no great effect. To morrow he has ordered to drink purging waters with manna or some other equivalent. Believe me my good friend I have had much ado to keep afoot the latter part off the summer. I wish I be able to doe the like this fall. I am now sensible that a constitution when once broke thoroughly, as mine has bin, can never be united again. The learned with all their skill can but make patched work on it. Within this fortnight I wrote twice to you and transcribed in each a long paragraph from a quondam friend off yours; since which I have not had a line from you, which makes me apprehensive one or both might have miscarried. By the same post I wrote to Peter to let you have the balance off your account but before he did it, that he should advise with the Guardian and have his
approbation, without which, as he is on the spott, I know it would be reckoned a presumption off the highest nature. I happened to fall in with Jimmy Clavering att the coffee house last Sunday; he told me that he had heard that Mr Pitt and the Lady were upon a close treaty with you, which he hoped would succeed. I replied that if they did not stand in their own light, I doubted not off your inclinations and ability to serve both the gentleman and lady. I hear George Oldner is upon his return, re infect . However his project has obliged the Sunderland owners to admeasure, whereas if I mistake not that was in a great measure disused off last year. I wrote lately to the Colonel about Farnacres and desired him to consider, now that he has a fair prospect off getting down a pitt about Christmas, if some provision should not be made out off Whickham top coal to help off with those stone coal, without which depend upon it they will not be marketable. I hope your Park water catchers have no diffidence off compassing what they proposed in relation to that concern. I again must repeat my thankfulness to you for all kind offers. What provocation was given the knight, att a late sitting, to abuse the honest chancellor to that degree? Has there bin any old grudge lying latent twixt them? No coals go off so currently all this year as Mr Pitt's . The dealers say that Bucks Nook comes fowl, which is occasioned by mixture; Hutton and Benwell much crestfallen; Main Team not much to be complained off; Clavering Stella in worse repute than ever, seldom comes within 13d off Team; the Grand Lease abominable; Scotswood and Felon att a low ebb; and Elswick not so much as once named. Our friends are still in Hertfordshire and don't return till middle off this month; I hear nothing off the motion of those from your quarters, they like their entertainment . But if the weather be the same with you as it is here, they will have reason to repent they did not move sooner. I always forget my self when I converse with you; I find no end till I come to that off my paper, which now calls on me to conclude ... P.S. The Regent seems very desirous off cultivating a strict friendship with us and there looks to be a good disposition towards peace in the north. When I can learn the certainty you shall hear further. However these have off a sudden raised stocks very high.
164 27th November 1716

I have bin confined to my house ever since my last to you, which was Saturday's post, and very ill I have bin and att present my spirits so sunk that I can scarce speak to be heard. Yet am sensible that a man off industry ought not to be balked. In relation to the affair off Morpeth and misapplication off the moneys for charitable uses, some honest gentlemen in the neighbourhood or substantial freeholder or inhabitant I believe might file a short bill off complaint against the managers, and if they can make out their allegations that very
charitable gift may be obliged to make good the charge off the suit. You know that my Lord can't be advised with because it may come before him; but I know a parallel case in some measure to this where the parties prosecuting succeeded. I was directed as most proper to take the opinion off some learned counsel, which is the best way off proceeding if as above or by information in the King's Bench. If you think proper, draw up the state off the case as full yet as brief as you can and I shall lay it before some able off the learned. To have his opinion will not cost above 2 guineas . As to your former enclosed I can't yet come att it to gratify your desire off having it returned, neither can I give you a farther insight than what has bin hitherto done. If you will take my notion tic this. Suppose you should get the gentleman who is willing to signify the substance off what he knows, without any name, transmitt it and I will lay it before you know who , who will be better able to judge off the merit. You know we are cautious how we promise, but when we have done, a punctual performance may be expected and above all a secrecy from that quarter may be depended upon. I need not enlarge. Pray is not a new undertaking near bottomed? Tic about the time proposed. Adieu ...
167 20th December 1716

I am obliged by your favour the last post, which had it brought better tidings off your health would have bin much more acceptable, though I think towards the end off the first paragraph you seem to prick up. Alas William , I am pestered with an old humour which haunts a great toe. I have bin in Small's hands almost every day this fortnight; you can't readily imagine the pain I undergo by having the nail even to the very root forced out, and the surgeon's design seems to leave me none. Besides his cutting and slashing, he never leaves me without an application off precipitate corrosive powders which keep me warm day and night: this last I did not sleep an hour from the time I went to bed till I rose this morning , and that is a melancholy ditty. The Colonel wrote me word off the coaling Farnacres and promised a further account in a post or two; nevertheless should be glad from time to time to hear from you the cracks off her. In answer to his I told him I expected to have a chaldron for a trial gratis (save I would pay freight) as soon as he had got well into her. In the next place must tell you that neither my father nor I ever heard a
syllable from Charles Waite on the subject; we had bin att his door two or 3 times, insomuch that I advised my father to send this morning to know what he had done in the matter. The answer was that he was wrote to to sue out the patent, for Mr Jenison I presume, but when he applied he found some other person had bin employed in that affair and that they had sent it down by Tuesday's post; by which I apprehend that Mr Ledgard must have miscarried. Had I not bin confined in a manner to the house by this toe I would have had from his own mouth the particulars. Mr Roper was the person sent, and he can neither receive nor bring an answer to satisfaction. No more on this till I am better informed from Charles himself, save that I am given to understand that the Gatekeeper Carr corrected the mistake by inserting Wolsington instead off Elswick, but these matters for your self. I delayed answering your quondam friend's for a fortnight att least and then did it in a few lines. The 4 names I sent to my friend this afternoon in a letter, since which have had no account than that it was delivered to his own hand and that is enough. One would think that an evil spirit was got into a brother off mine. My father had an account off it before but chose to conceal it. You have business enough for a dozen off tolerable heads on your hands besides that off the public. We are all mortal and suppose you should drop, would not your family be strangely bewildered? Could Mr Mayor entail on his posterity his head and genius in business well and good, but when all is don experience is a great matter. Excuse this freedom, which comes from him that is not capable off advising, yet is a perfect well wisher to you and yours. Adieu ... P.S. We don't know what to think off the dismission off Lord Townsend. The Torys crow. Mrs Mountagu having obtained a commission off lunacy against her husband, the commissioners met this day. I heard her council. By what passed it is guessd'd she will prove him such.
